newsitem.title: UK: UK'S AIRTOURS FALLS ON PROFIT TAKING.
newsitem.headline: UK'S AIRTOURS FALLS ON PROFIT TAKING.

text.p: Shares in British travel operator Airtours Plc fell on Wednesday as profit takers moved in following the company's third quarter pre-tax profits.
"They were reasonable results," said Julian Easthope, leisure analyst at UBS. "They would have been good had the U.S. side not dipped".
By 1115 GMT, shares in the leisure company fell 28-1/2p, just over two percent, to 12.00-1/2 stg.
The stock has more than doubled in value over the last twelve months. A year ago today the stock was trading at 569p.
Earlier the company announced pre-tax profits of 24.08 million stg for the three months to June 30 compared to 19.34 million a year ago.
The dividend was raised to 4.0p from 3.25p whilst turnover rose to 574.39 million stg compared to 485.23 million stg the previous year.

The company's North American Leisure Group meanwhile, reported a loss before tax of 3.6 million stg. Cumulative losses of 4.8 million stg over the nine month period compared to a profit of 3.3 million stg in the same period last year.
